text:
incident-bot: 🔔 HOT: eu-west-1 gpu-pool reporting sustained saturation. queue_length=1,340 (warn=200), avg_wait=24s. Autoscaler: repeated placement errors. Paging @sre-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-surge

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. Pulling placement traces and queue dumps. Any customer tickets yet?

maria.g: We're seeing spikes of 429s and 503s across /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints for medium+ models. p99 token latency up ~8x for some tenants. Dashboard: https://console.internal/dash/alpha

ryan.l: Autoscaler log sample shows repeated "fit failure" and "quota prevented node creation" errors. Snippet below:

```
E0520 14:03:11 placement.go:210] FitFailure: pool eu-west-1-prod: need_contiguous_slices=4; host_slice_map=[2,2,1,1] -> no fit
W0520 14:03:27 autoscaler.go:498] scaleUp aborted: provider.quotaExceeded region=eu-west-1
I0520 14:03:42 placement.go:322] placement rejected: MIGTemplateMismatch(templateA vs templateB) - pod requests 4-slice binding
```

eng-runtime: We rolled a partial MIG template change last night that converted a subset of hosts to 2-slice topology for thermal testing. Binpacker hasn't run repack and scheduler still prefers exact 4-slice matches, so many GPUs are idle but unusable for 4-slice pods -> stranded capacity.

infra-ops: Cloud shows ~22 idle GPUs across 7 nodes but each is configured as 2-slice only. Pending pods request 4-slice. Also we've hit regional hard quota for GPU count; provider request CP-11400 sent.

product-support: Multiple P1s opening. Main customer call: DataWave Analytics reporting timeouts on long-context jobs. Ticket: CS-4012 escalated.

solutions: Notified impacted enterprise contacts. They're asking whether we can route them to another region (us-east-1) temporarily.

sre-oncall: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) enable best-effort model downgrade for queued requests (4-slice -> 2-slice where acceptable). 2) throttle and shed non-critical ingestion (reduce new low-priority queued work). 3) trigger emergency repack job / force-launch legacy-template nodes if quota allows. 4) cross-region routing for enterprise fallbacks. Thoughts?

maria.g: Implementing step 1 canary now for non-enterprise tenants (5%). Patching routing and admission.

ryan.l: Posting quick admission rule we pushed to gate substitution:

```
- id: best-effort-downgrade
  match: tenant.tier != "enterprise" and request.model in ["redwood-4s-pro","redwood-4s-med"]
  condition: request.queue_time > 7s
  action: substitute_model -> "redwood-2s-quant"
```

eng-runtime: Canary started. Also adding a token-level throttling rule to slow low-priority batch submissions to prevent queue growth.

infra-ops: Starting cordon/drain of eu-batch-lowprio to free 2-slice hosts: `kubectl cordon node/eu-batch-* && kubectl drain node/eu-batch-* --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Expect to free ~12 2-slice GPUs.

incident-bot: Autoscaler still emitting: "scaleUp attempt: rejected due to quotaHardLimit" — provider ticket CP-11400 created (state=Pending).

maria.g: After the canary downgrade, non-enterprise error rate dropped ~22% on affected routes. p95 improved from ~3.6s -> 2.5s. Queue still high (~820).

ryan.l: Some batch jobs are marked preempt=false and cannot be drained. Requesting authorization to terminate 4 longest-running, lowest-priority jobs (grace=30s). Approve?

sre-oncall: Approve manual termination for those 4 jobs to free capacity. Document job IDs and owners.

infra-ops: Manual kill completed for 4 jobs, freed 8 2-slice GPUs. New free slices visible but scheduler still failing to place 4-slice pods because contiguous slices aren't available.

eng-runtime: Deploying a temporary scheduler fallback that will allow co-scheduling two 2-slice devices on the same pod as an emergency packing strategy. This requires driver binding changes and is enabled as a toggle. Doing a dry-run on a canary node.

product-support: Asking for permission to move a small set of enterprise tenants to us-east fallback. Some accepted; DataWave wants migration for critical workloads only.

solutions: Coordinating migration windows with customers. Starting the migration of DataWave critical traffic at 14:40 UTC (50% -> 100% over 4 minutes).

incident-bot: Note: manual quota bump still pending with provider. If CP-11400 not approved in 20m, we should prefer emergency mixed-template nodes.

ryan.l: We observed that the autoscaler also refused to create mixed-template nodes because of a quota guard inside our cluster autoscaler that denies mismatched template groups. I'm proposing a temporary override to allow creating one legacy 4-slice node group while waiting on quota. Requesting infra lead approval.

infra-ops: Approved one-time ops-override for emergency node creation if cloud permits. Starting legacy node group spin-up now.

incident-bot: ACTION: emergency nodegroup request initiated (legacy-4s), cloud responded: 4 nodes provisioning (16 GPUs).

maria.g: After emergency nodes started coming online, pending pods began scheduling. Queue dropped from ~820 -> ~120 in ~8 minutes. Latency improved across most routes.

eng-runtime: The emergency co-scheduling toggle worked for a handful of backfilled pods but we prefer to revert this complex driver change after stable remediation. We'll keep the toggle on for 90 minutes then revert.

product-support: DataWave reports critical job success; other customers show degraded but acceptable performance. We're drafting a customer-facing incident summary and offering support credits for affected windows.

solutions: Confirmed migrations: DataWave critical traffic moved successfully to us-east fallback; remaining enterprise customers in talks.

ryan.l: Post-incident immediate actions we should take: 1) roll back partial MIG template if possible; 2) run a forced binpacker repack to consolidate slices; 3) add a preflight gate to MIG rollouts that verifies downstream allocator compatibility; 4) add quota-forecast alerts when used/limit > 0.85.

infra-ops: Opening follow-up infra tickets: INF-3019 (quota coordination + provider escalation), INF-3020 (node-template rollback plan).

sre-oncall: I'll remain on until queue < 100 and emergency nodes stable. Morning oncall (ryan.l) will take over at 07:30 UTC. Please add step-by-step runbook notes to the incident doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATE: mitigated -> watching. Tags: gpu, autoscaler, MIG-template, stranded-capacity, quota, emergency-nodegroup. Postmortem required.

maria.g: Adding metric: stranded_slices_ratio = idle_incompatible_slices / total_gpu_count. Alert at 0.08 and page at 0.15. Also adding early-warning quota forecast alert.

eng-runtime: We'll prepare a quick patch to binpacker to prefer repacking in presence of mixed slice topologies and test in staging. Plan to automate repack job after MIG rollouts.

product-support: Sending customer blast now with restoration and mitigation summary. Recording list of impacted tenants for credits.

sre-oncall: Thanks everyone. Log any remaining notes in https://redwood.internal/incidents/6110005555 and start the postmortem draft. Handoff to Ryan at 07:30 UTC.

ryan.l: Will own postmortem. Proposed remediations: template preflight check, slice-aware scheduler/binpacker, quota forecasting alerts, and an API flag for model graceful degradation.

incident-bot: Watchers added: eng-runtime, infra-ops, product-support. Watch state active. Page if anything regresses.
